review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:

Projected to score 72.8, they scored 64 (−8.8 points, 12% under); projected to allow 79.7, they allowed 66 (−13.7 points, 17% under).

Projected to score 79.7, they scored 66 (−13.7 points, 17% under); projected to allow 72.8, they allowed 64 (−8.8 points, 12% under).

The bigger miss was Billikens' scoring (-13.7 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations

Total: 130 against 152.5 projected (-22.5), about the 6th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.834 of the raw projection. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 1175 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.978 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Cardinal attack ×0.965, defense ×0.969 (9 games); Billikens attack ×1.000, defense ×0.994 (7 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
